national.title: How to Get a Learner's Licence in India (2026)
national.summary: Step-by-step guide to applying for a Learner Licence online on the Sarathi Parivahan portal. Verified statutory fee of ₹200, required documents, and computerized test instructions.

steps.title: Submit Form 2 on the Sarathi Parivahan Portal
steps.description: Visit parivahan.gov.in and select your State. Click 'Apply for Learner Licence' and select your vehicle class.
steps.calloutText: Choosing Aadhaar authentication allows paperless online verification without visiting an RTO office in most states.

steps.title: Select Aadhaar Authentication Mode
steps.description: Choose 'Submit via Aadhaar Authentication' if your mobile is linked to Aadhaar. Otherwise, choose physical submission at your RTO.

steps.title: Upload Required Documents and Photo
steps.description: Upload scanned age proof, address proof, and Form 1 fitness self-declaration. Non-Aadhaar applicants must also upload photograph and signature.

steps.title: Pay Government Fee Online (₹200)
steps.description: Pay the statutory fee of ₹150 for application processing and ₹50 for test fee. Pay via net banking, debit card, or UPI.
steps.calloutText: Print the e-receipt immediately. The transaction number is needed if payment status enters pending.

steps.title: Watch the Mandatory Road Safety Tutorial Video
steps.description: Log in to Sarathi and watch the official road safety video tutorial. The computerized test unlocks only after watching this video.

steps.title: Take the Computerized Learner Test (LL Test)
steps.description: Answer 15 multiple-choice questions on road signs and traffic rules within 30 seconds each. You must score 11 out of 15 to pass.
steps.where: Online from Home (with webcam) or at RTO Lab

steps.title: Download and Print Your Digital Learner Licence (Form 3)
steps.description: Your digital Learner Licence in Form 3 is generated immediately upon passing. Download the PDF and keep a physical printout for driving practice.
steps.calloutText: Vehicles driven by learner licence holders must display red 'L' plates on front and back.

rejectionReasons.title: Name or Date of Birth Mismatch on Aadhaar
rejectionReasons.description: If the name on your 10th marksheet or birth certificate does not match the name returned by Aadhaar e-KYC, the application is halted.
rejectionReasons.solution: Update your Aadhaar details first at an Aadhaar Seva Kendra, or apply via non-Aadhaar mode with physical document scrutiny at the RTO.

rejectionReasons.title: Failing the Computerized Road Signs and Rules Test
rejectionReasons.description: Scoring below 11 out of 15 questions leads to test failure on the computerized exam.
rejectionReasons.solution: Review traffic signs and road regulations on Sarathi practice tests, then book a re-test after paying ₹50.

rejectionReasons.title: Missing Form 1A Medical Certificate for Applicants Aged 40+
rejectionReasons.description: Applicants aged 40 or older who submit without a registered doctor signed Form 1A are rejected at scrutiny.
rejectionReasons.solution: Get Form 1A signed by a registered MBBS medical doctor with doctor registration stamp.

rejectionReasons.title: Missing Parent Consent for Minor Applicants Aged 16 to 18
rejectionReasons.description: Minor applicants applying for non-gear vehicles without parent declaration will be rejected.
rejectionReasons.solution: Have your parent or legal guardian sign the consent section on application Form 2.

rejectionReasons.title: Blurry or Incomplete Document Scans
rejectionReasons.description: Uploading unreadable documents or cropped certificates leads to application rejection by the scrutiny clerk.
rejectionReasons.solution: Re-scan the original documents clearly in PDF format under 200 KB before uploading.

rejectionReasons.title: Applying Outside Your Residential RTO Jurisdiction
rejectionReasons.description: Selecting an RTO that does not cover your residential pin code leads to cancellation at document scrutiny.
rejectionReasons.solution: Check your district RTO jurisdiction list and select the office matching your residential address.

faqItems.question: What is the minimum age to apply for a Learner Licence in India?
faqItems.answer: The minimum age is 16 years for gearless two-wheelers up to 50cc. It is 18 years for geared motorcycles and cars.

faqItems.question: Can I take the Learner Licence test from home?
faqItems.answer: Yes. States offering Aadhaar e-KYC allow you to take the computerized test from home using a webcam.

faqItems.question: What is the passing mark for the computerized Learner test?
faqItems.answer: You must score at least 11 correct answers out of 15 questions to pass the computerized learner test.

faqItems.question: How long is a Learner's Licence valid in India?
faqItems.answer: A Learner's Licence is valid for exactly 6 months (180 days) from the date of issue across all states and Union Territories.

faqItems.question: Can I drive alone on public roads with a Learner's Licence?
faqItems.answer: No. You must be accompanied by someone who holds a valid permanent driving licence for that vehicle class.

faqItems.question: What should I do if I fail the online Learner test?
faqItems.answer: You can pay a re-test fee of ₹50 on Sarathi and reappear for the test after 24 hours.

faqItems.question: When can I apply for a permanent driving licence after getting my learner licence?
faqItems.answer: You can apply for a permanent driving licence after 30 days from your Learner Licence issue date.

faqItems.question: What is the official statutory fee for a Learner Licence?
faqItems.answer: The statutory fee is ₹150 for application processing plus ₹50 for the test fee, totaling ₹200 for a single vehicle class.

items.title: Working Webcam and Stable Internet
items.description: Ensure your computer has an active camera with good lighting for facial recognition proctoring.

items.title: Application Number and Password
items.description: Keep your Sarathi application number and SMS login password ready before launching the test.

items.title: Review Road Signs and Rules
items.description: Revise mandatory, cautionary, and informatory traffic signs before beginning the timed 15-question test.

items.title: Original Aadhaar Card
items.description: Keep your original physical Aadhaar card beside you for identity confirmation during testing.

items.title: Quiet Room with No Background Movement
items.description: Sit alone in a quiet room because the proctoring camera flags any background persons or movement.

GJ.title: How to Apply for Learner's Licence in Gujarat (2026)
GJ.summary: Gujarat provides contactless online Learner Licence services with home-based computerized testing through Sarathi Parivahan and Digital Gujarat. Citizens can also take the computerized test in Gujarati at designated government Industrial Training Institutes.
GJ.verifiedBy: Civic Research Editorial Team - Gujarat Bureau

steps.title: Access Sarathi Gujarat Portal with Aadhaar Authentication
steps.description: Select Gujarat state on Sarathi Parivahan and choose applicant with Aadhaar for contactless application without visiting the RTO office.
steps.calloutText: Aadhaar e-KYC automatically imports verified demographic details and waives mandatory physical document verification at the RTO.

steps.title: Complete Online Form 2 and Upload Signatures
steps.description: Select vehicle classes such as Motorcycle Without Gear or Light Motor Vehicle. Upload digital signature and emergency contact blood group.

steps.title: Pay Gujarat Statutory Fees via Cyber Treasury
steps.description: Pay one hundred fifty rupees test fee and fifty rupees per vehicle category using the integrated Gujarat Cyber Treasury payment gateway.
steps.calloutText: Total statutory fee is two hundred rupees for one vehicle class or three hundred fifty rupees for both two-wheeler and car.

steps.title: Complete Road Safety Awareness Video Tutorial
steps.description: Watch the mandatory road safety tutorial video on Sarathi Gujarat. The portal verifies video completion before unlocking the computer test.
steps.calloutText: You cannot start the online LL exam until the portal registers 100% completion of the road safety tutorial.

steps.title: Appear for Computerized LL Test at Home or ITI
steps.description: Take the 15-question multiple choice test in Gujarati, Hindi, or English using your home webcam or visit a designated Gujarat ITI center.
steps.where: Home (Webcam Proctoring) or Nearest Gujarat ITI Center
steps.calloutText: Score at least 11 correct answers out of 15 questions within the 48-second timer per question to qualify.

steps.title: Instantly Download Digital Gujarat Learner Licence
steps.description: Upon scoring eleven or more marks, download the official Form 3 Learner Licence PDF directly from the portal or DigiLocker.
steps.calloutText: Your Gujarat Learner Licence is valid across India for six months from the date of passing.

faqItems.question: Can I take the Gujarat Learner Licence test in Gujarati?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The computerized test questions and audio are available in Gujarati, Hindi, and English.

faqItems.question: Can I take the LL test from home without visiting an RTO in Gujarat?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Gujarat enables 100% contactless testing from home using Aadhaar authentication and webcam proctoring.

faqItems.question: What if I do not have a computer or webcam at home?
faqItems.answer: You can take the test at any authorized Gujarat Government Industrial Training Institute (ITI) or RTO office.

faqItems.question: What is the passing score for the Gujarat LL computerized test?
faqItems.answer: You must answer at least 11 questions correctly out of 15 questions to pass the test.
